title: How to save as a video in PowerPoint on Mac: MP4 steps for Microsoft 365
metaTitle: How to Save as a Video in PowerPoint on Mac: MP4 Steps
description: How to save as a video in PowerPoint on Mac: open File > Export, choose MP4 or MOV, pick a quality, and select Export. Steps for Microsoft 365.
targetKeyword: how to save as a video in powerpoint on mac
intro: On a Mac, PowerPoint makes a video through File > Export, not Save As. Choose MP4 or MOV, pick a quality, keep recorded narration on if you have it, then select Export.
tldr: Use File > Export on your Mac. Save As does not offer video options.
In the File Format list, choose MP4 or MOV, then pick a quality from Ultra HD (4K) down to Standard (480p).
Record narration first, then keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked when you export.
Animations do not play in the video, and PowerPoint for the web cannot make an MP4.
If no video option appears, check your version under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint and your license.

blocks.text: Use File > Export, not Save As

Save As will not make a video. The Save As dialog does not offer video options, so it is the wrong route. Go to File > Export instead. That menu opens the dialog where you choose a video format and a quality setting. Microsoft's Mac instructions start from this same menu, so follow that path.

The shortcut is a trap. ⌘⇧S opens Save As, which does not help with video. Microsoft's keyboard shortcut list for Mac gives no shortcut for Export, and none for Record Slide Show either. You will use the menu bar for both. That is fine, because the menu path is short and easy to repeat.
Check your PowerPoint version before you start

The export feature depends on your version. Microsoft's Mac page gives PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac version 15.23 or later as the requirement. The same page says recorded narration is included in exported video from version 16.19. PowerPoint 2019 for Mac also needs 16.19 or later. Treat 15.23 as the old minimum and 16.19 as the practical one.

To check your version, choose PowerPoint > About PowerPoint. The current Mac build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3, released Oct 27, 2026. Those notes describe quality and performance work. The recent entries do not mention export or video, so check your version and license before you update.

A 2018 Microsoft Q&A thread describes another cause. That user was on PowerPoint for Mac 15.41 and could not find Create Video under File > Export. The most helpful reply said the feature needs an Office 365 Subscription license, and that Volume License installs lack it. The thread is old and was contested, so confirm your license before you rely on it.
Choose MP4 or MOV for the file

The File Format list offers MP4 and MOV. Pick MP4 when the video will leave your Mac, for a shared drive, a web upload, or a colleague on Windows. MOV suits a file that stays with Macs and QuickTime. It does the same job for playback on your own machine.

Here is a worked example. You have a sales deck with a voice track, and the video must go onto an internal portal that colleagues open on Windows. Choose MP4, pick Full HD (1080p), and keep narration on. If the portal rejects the file, ask the admin which format it accepts, then export again rather than editing the deck.
Pick a quality setting for where the video goes

The Quality list offers four settings: Ultra HD (4K), Full HD (1080p), HD (720p), and Standard (480p). Higher settings give sharper slides and larger files. Lower settings give smaller files that are easier to send and store.

Match the setting to the screen. A deck for a large projector deserves Full HD (1080p) or Ultra HD (4K). A deck for a phone or a quick email can use HD (720p) or Standard (480p). Ultra HD (4K) is rarely needed for a short narrated clip, and it makes the file bigger. Export one test copy first, then check its size before you export the final version.
Record narration and timings before you export

Export uses the timings and narration that PowerPoint has stored in the deck. If you have not recorded anything, each slide stays on screen for the same time. Choose Slide Show > Record Slide Show to add narration and set a timing for each slide. Once you finish, those timings and narration are part of the file, ready for export.

Keep the checkbox Use Recorded Timings and Narrations ticked in the export dialog. Narration recorded in Slide Show plays in the video. Other embedded media files do not, so the recorded narration is the audio that carries through. For the full recording steps, read [how to record a slide show in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/record-a-slide-show-in-powerpoint).
What does not make it into the video

Some parts of a deck do not survive the export. Animation effects do not play at all. Several transitions play differently in the video than on screen. Embedded media, other than recorded narration, does not play. Check each of these before you blame the export or the file.

items: Animation effects, which do not play at all in the exported video.
Embedded media, other than narration recorded in Slide Show.
Transitions, several of which look different from the live slide show.
Slides without timings, which each stay on screen for the same time.

blocks.text: If your slides depend on motion, rebuild the key moments as separate slides, or add the motion in a video editor after export. Test one slide first. A short test export shows the problem sooner than a full deck will.
Why PowerPoint for the web cannot make an MP4

PowerPoint for the web does not export to MP4. Microsoft's web features page lists Download As options of .pptx, .pdf, .odp, and JPEG images, one image per slide. Video is not on that list. A Microsoft Community answer says the same thing, and it gives the workaround: download the file and open it in the desktop app.

The web version also limits media. Microsoft says it won't insert large media files, citing a limit of 50 to 100 MB for embedded media and 100 KB for WAV files. If a clip or sound file is larger than that, fix it in the desktop app before you export from there.
When the export dialog has no video option

Work through three checks in order. First, confirm you are in the desktop app, not a browser tab. Second, check the version under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint. Third, check the license, because the 2018 thread links the missing option to Volume License installs.

If the license is the problem, the fix sits with whoever manages your Microsoft account, such as your IT team. Ask them which Microsoft 365 license your Mac uses, and whether it includes the export feature. Bring the version number from About PowerPoint so they can answer faster.
Fallback: record the slides with the Mac screen recorder

A community answer on Microsoft Q&A describes a workaround. Play the slides full screen, press ⌘⇧5 to start a screen recording, and press ⌘⌃Esc to stop it. The file saves as a .mov. That answer does not name a converter, so you need to convert the file to .mp4 yourself with a tool you trust, if MP4 is required.

Treat this as a fallback, not a Microsoft method. The recording captures what the screen shows, so timing depends on how you run the slides. Video quality depends on your display. Keep the original deck, so you can run a proper export later when the license or version is fixed.
Check the file before you share it

Open the exported file in QuickTime Player, or double-click it in Finder. Watch the whole video once, with sound on. Compare the narration and slide timing with your deck. Look for missing animations and for any slide that appears cut off or in the wrong order.

Then think about where it goes. A 4K file can be large, so check the size before you upload it and compare it with any limit the platform lists. If the platform rejects the file, export again at a lower quality setting rather than cutting slides from the deck.
Common mistakes to avoid

items: Using Save As and then wondering why no video option appears.
Forgetting to tick Use Recorded Timings and Narrations after recording narration.
Exporting from PowerPoint for the web, which cannot make an MP4.
Expecting animations and embedded videos to show up in the finished file.
Choosing Ultra HD (4K) for every file, then sharing a large video that nobody needs in that quality.

blocks.text: Where to go next

Once the video works, you may want speaker notes for a live talk. The guide on [adding speaker notes in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/add-speaker-notes-in-powerpoint) covers that. If your slides are the wrong shape for the screen you plan to use, change the slide size before you record, so you only record once.

faq.question: Can I save a PowerPoint presentation as a video on Mac with Save As?
faq.answer: No. Save As does not offer video options on Mac. Use File > Export, then choose MP4 or MOV in the File Format list and select Export.

faq.question: Which should I choose, MP4 or MOV?
faq.answer: Choose MP4 when the video will leave your Mac, such as for a shared drive, a web upload, or a colleague on Windows. MOV suits a file that stays on Macs.

faq.question: Does the exported video include my narration?
faq.answer: Yes, if you recorded it with Slide Show > Record Slide Show and Use Recorded Timings and Narrations is ticked. Microsoft says narration is included from PowerPoint for Mac version 16.19.

faq.question: Can PowerPoint for the web export a video?
faq.answer: Not to MP4. Microsoft's web features page lists .pptx, .pdf, .odp, and JPEG for Download As. Download the file and export it from the desktop app.

faq.question: Why do my animations disappear in the video?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Mac export page says animation effects do not play at all in the exported video. Rebuild key moments as separate slides, or add motion in a video editor after export.

faq.question: Why is there no Export as Video option on my Mac?
faq.answer: Check your version under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint and your license. A 2018 Microsoft thread says Volume License installs lack the feature, though that thread was contested.

faq.question: Can I make a video from a deck if Export is unavailable?
faq.answer: You can use the Mac screen recorder as a fallback. Press ⌘⇧5 to record, then ⌘⌃Esc to stop. The file saves as .mov, so convert it to .mp4 if you need MP4.

faq.question: Which quality setting should I pick?
faq.answer: The options are Ultra HD (4K), Full HD (1080p), HD (720p), and Standard (480p). Pick Full HD (1080p) for most screens and projectors, and a lower setting when the file must be small.

task: Save a PowerPoint presentation as a video on Mac
appliesTo: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, version 16.19 or later
requirements: PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, version 16.19 or later, for narration in the video
The desktop app on your Mac. PowerPoint for the web cannot export MP4.
A license that includes the export feature. Check License under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint.
Finished slides, plus any narration or timings you want in the video
Enough free disk space for the exported file

steps.name: Open the finished deck in the desktop app
steps.text: Open the presentation in PowerPoint for Mac, not in a browser. Finish your slides, images, and fonts before you export. The export uses the deck as it is at that moment.
steps.tip: If the file opened in a browser, download it and open the copy in the desktop app.

steps.name: Confirm your version and license
steps.text: Choose PowerPoint > About PowerPoint and note the version number. You want 16.19 or later if the video needs narration. Check the license entry in the same window.
steps.tip: Microsoft's Mac page lists 15.23 as the older minimum, so 16.19 is the safer target.

steps.name: Record narration and timings if you need them
steps.text: Choose Slide Show > Record Slide Show. Record your narration and timings slide by slide. Without a recording, each slide shows for the same time.
steps.tip: Record in a quiet room, and test your microphone before you start.

steps.name: Open the Export dialog
steps.text: Choose File > Export. Do not choose Save As, because it does not offer video options and its shortcut is ⌘⇧S.
steps.tip: Microsoft lists no keyboard shortcut for Export on Mac, so use the menu.

steps.name: Pick MP4 or MOV
steps.text: In the File Format list, choose MP4 if the video will leave your Mac. Choose MOV if it stays on Macs.
steps.tip: If you are unsure, MP4 is the safer choice to share.

steps.name: Choose a quality setting
steps.text: Open the Quality list. Pick Ultra HD (4K), Full HD (1080p), HD (720p), or Standard (480p). Full HD (1080p) suits most projectors and screens. Use a lower setting when the file has to be small.
steps.tip: Export one test copy at a lower setting first to check the size.

steps.name: Keep recorded timings and narration on
steps.text: If you recorded narration or timings, keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked. Turn it off only if you want the video to ignore your recording.

steps.name: Select Export and save the file
steps.text: Select Export, choose a folder, and save the file. Wait for the export to finish before you quit PowerPoint or move the file.
steps.tip: Keep the original .pptx. You can export again later with different settings.

steps.name: Play the video and check it
steps.text: Open the file in QuickTime Player, or double-click it in Finder. Watch the whole video with sound on. Check the narration, slide timing, and transitions against your deck.
steps.tip: Animations will not appear, so plan for that before you share.

shortcuts.action: Save As (the wrong route for video)

troubleshooting.fix: Confirm you are in the desktop app and check PowerPoint > About PowerPoint. A 2018 thread linked the missing option to Volume License installs, so check your license with IT or your Microsoft account owner.

troubleshooting.problem: Narration is missing from the video
troubleshooting.fix: Check that you recorded with Slide Show > Record Slide Show, that Use Recorded Timings and Narrations is ticked, and that your version is 16.19 or later.

troubleshooting.problem: Animations or some embedded media do not play
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected. Animations do not play at all, and other embedded media does not either. Rebuild key moments as slides, or add the clip in a video editor after export.

troubleshooting.problem: Every slide stays on screen for the same time
troubleshooting.fix: Set timings or record the slide show. Without recorded timings, each slide holds for the same time.

troubleshooting.problem: PowerPoint for the web offers no MP4
troubleshooting.fix: Download the file, open it in PowerPoint for Mac, and export from File > Export.

troubleshooting.problem: The fallback recording saves as .mov, not .mp4
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected with the Mac screen recorder. Convert the file to MP4 with a tool you trust, or share the MOV if the recipient can play it.
